units.intent: A narrow, process-wide hook so an embedding application can observe JSON parse/serialize timing and document size, without the JSON package depending on that application.

objects.name: MetricsOperation
objects.role: PARSE or SERIALIZE

objects.name: MetricsObserver
objects.role: callback signature

objects.name: setMetricsObserver
objects.role: installs/replaces the callback; nullptr disables reporting

objects.name: reportMetrics
objects.role: invoked by Parser/Writer after each operation to notify the observer, if set

objects.name: (anonymous namespace) metricsObserver
objects.role: atomic<MetricsObserver> backing storage; not declared in the header

units.intent: Parse a JSON string into a JSON::Value tree, in a strict mode that throws on malformed input and a permissive mode that does not.

objects.name: Parser
objects.role: two static entry points, read() (throws JSON::InvalidArgument) and readUnsafe() (swallows parse errors), both driving a rapidjson::Reader over a SAXHandler

naming_quality.note: readUnsafe clearly signals the risk relative to read

units.intent: Implements rapidjson's SAX handler interface to build a JSON::Value tree (with nested objects/arrays) from the callback stream a rapidjson::Reader emits while parsing.

objects.name: SAXHandler
objects.role: implements the full rapidjson handler surface (Null/Bool/Int/Uint/Int64/Uint64/Double/String/StartObject/Key/EndObject/StartArray/EndArray/RawNumber), tracks a stack of in-progress Value contexts, hands off the finished root via getValue()

objects.name: SAXHandler::endContext
objects.role: pops the current context and, inside an array, stages the next placeholder element

name_fit.note: matches the rapidjson SAX handler convention it implements

naming_quality.note: interface names are fixed by rapidjson's contract; root is a manually new/deleted raw pointer later wrapped in a unique_ptr on hand-off, an ownership pattern worth a second look though not a naming issue

units.intent: A CRTP base that documents and compile-time-enforces a toJSON()/fromJSON() contract on a derived type, without a vtable, so the derived type stays an aggregate.

objects.name: Serializable<Derived>
objects.role: base toJSON()/fromJSON() are static_assert stubs that fire only if the derived class fails to hide them via name hiding

objects.name: always_false_v<T>
objects.role: delays the static_assert failure to instantiation time

location_fit.note: a JSON-serialization contract helper, reasonably grouped here even though the CRTP trick itself is generic C++, not JSON-specific; no in-repo consumer currently derives from it

naming_quality.note: always_false_v follows established standard-library-style naming for this trait helper

units.intent: Static helpers for reading, merging, stripping, and sanitizing JSON::Value trees (key replace/strip/patch, path<->object conversion, transport-safe string sanitizing) used across Bedrock and consuming applications.

objects.name: Utils
objects.role: static utility class holding shared singleton JSON::Value constants and tree-manipulation helpers; no instance state

objects.name: Utils::EMPTY_OBJECT/EMPTY_ARRAY/NULL_VALUE/FALSE_VALUE/TRUE_VALUE/EMPTY_STRING/ZERO_INT_VALUE/MAX_INT_VALUE/ZERO_FLOAT_VALUE
objects.role: shared singleton JSON::Value constants reused to avoid repeated construction

objects.name: Utils::sanitizeJSONStringForTransport
objects.role: hand-rolled UTF-8 validator/control-byte stripper for outbound JSON strings

misfits.why: doc comment is written entirely in terms of one caller's domain (bankAccounts.additionalData, apiResult, errorAttemptsCount, assetReport) and names an external test (GetWithdrawalAccountsTest) not present in this repo; the algorithm is generic but the documentation ties a package the README describes as application-agnostic to one consumer's onyx-merge use case

name_fit.note: generic JSON-tree utility grab-bag fits its name

naming_quality.note: clear camelCase methods; class name Utils is a generic catch-all but scoped under JSON:: so it doesn't collide with the repo's S-prefixed shared-utility convention

units.intent: Declares and implements JSON::Value, Bedrock's in-memory JSON document node (scalar, array, or object), including its exception hierarchy and small helper types for building and iterating it.

objects.name: JSON::Error
objects.role: base exception for JSON errors; captures a stack trace via SException

objects.name: JSON::TypeError
objects.role: thrown when a Value is accessed/cast as the wrong ValueType

objects.name: JSON::NotFound
objects.role: thrown when a keyed or indexed member does not exist

objects.name: JSON::InvalidArgument
objects.role: thrown for malformed caller input, e.g. a non-numeric path key

objects.name: JSON::ValueType
objects.role: discriminates which kind of JSON node a Value currently holds

objects.name: JSON::Value
objects.role: tagged-union JSON node: scalar storage plus shared_ptr-backed object/array storage and all accessors/mutators

objects.name: JSON::KeyValue
objects.role: move-only key/value pair used to build a Value object from an initializer_list

objects.name: JSON::_ArrayValue<T>
objects.role: adapter giving a Value's array begin()/end() for range-based for loops

objects.name: JSON::_ObjectValue<T>
objects.role: adapter giving a Value's object begin()/end() for range-based for loops

objects.name: JSON::ArrayValue / ConstArrayValue
objects.role: _ArrayValue<Value> / _ArrayValue<const Value>

objects.name: JSON::ObjectValue / ConstObjectValue
objects.role: _ObjectValue<Value> / _ObjectValue<const Value>

objects.name: JSON::logStackTraceOnEnsureTypeFailure
objects.role: thread_local debug flag toggling stack-trace logging on ensureType() failure

objects.name: operator<<(ostream&, const Value&)
objects.role: serializes a Value to a stream

misfits.why: mutable global-ish thread_local debug/diagnostics toggle declared inline in the core value-type header; reads like a logging switch, not part of the JSON data model
a generic JSON value type's merge API names a specific downstream consumer (SQLite) in its parameter; the behavior it selects is really just RFC 7386 JSON Merge Patch semantics
constructor-timing instrumentation adds a chrono::time_point member to every Value instance, even scalars that never touch it, purely to detect occasional slow map/vector-based construction
grants SAXHandler direct access to Value's private storage for fast construction; the source comment itself calls this out as 'Coupling++'

name_fit.note: core type is JSON::Value, but the file also carries the exception hierarchy, KeyValue, and the array/object range adapters, none named after Value

location_fit.note: sits correctly alongside Parser, Writer, SAXHandler, and Utils in libstuff/JSON

naming_quality.note: public API is descriptive and consistent; private members lack the repo's `_` prefix convention, and intValue/uintValue are two easily-confused fields disambiguated only by usingUnsigned

units.intent: A JSON serializer: build a document incrementally via an object/array cursor over rapidjson::Writer, or convert a whole JSON::Value tree to a string in one call (compact or pretty).

objects.name: Writer
objects.role: wraps rapidjson::Writer<StringBuffer>; instance API drives incremental construction, static serialize()/serializePretty() walk an existing JSON::Value tree directly

objects.name: Writer::serialize(value, writer)
objects.role: recursively walks a JSON::Value and feeds it to any rapidjson writer type; shared by serialize() and serializePretty()

naming_quality.note: consistent startX/endX pairs; private writeValue overloads appropriately hidden behind public templates
